headline: `b.backup.localStorage` legacy alias removed — use `b.backup.diskStorage`
summary: v0.11.2 renamed the local-filesystem backup backend from `b.backup.localStorage(opts)` to `b.backup.diskStorage(opts)` to keep the operator-facing surface unambiguous against Node 26's new `localStorage` global. v0.11.2 shipped the rename with a one-time deprecation warning routed through `b.deprecate.alias` and a tentative `removeIn: 0.12.0` to give operators a clean upgrade window. v0.11.20 removes the alias entirely — pre-v1 the project's stated policy is no backwards-compat shims (operators upgrade across breaking changes), and removing the alias now avoids tying the cleanup to the Node 26 floor-bump bundle later this year. Update any call site that still imports the legacy name; the underlying primitive's behavior and options are unchanged.

items.title: `b.backup.localStorage` — the legacy alias is gone
items.body: The property no longer resolves on `b.backup` and the one-time deprecation warning is no longer emitted. Migration is a literal-name find-and-replace: `b.backup.localStorage({ root: ... })` becomes `b.backup.diskStorage({ root: ... })`. The returned storage backend object, its options shape, and its wire contract with `b.backupBundle.create` are unchanged. See SECURITY.md's Node 26 compatibility section for the original rename rationale.
